propositions: The review-bot's /webhook and /rerun endpoints accept authentication tokens as query parameters, which uvicorn's default access log records in plaintext to stderr and journald.
The webhook token defaults to GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN when WEBHOOK_TOKEN is unset, making the exposed credential sufficient to drive reviews and authenticate as the bot against Gerrit.

The exposed token in journald and shared log excerpts represents a fail-open security exposure with no alarming or error signal, and any new token is logged on first use unless the underlying mechanism is fixed.

The fix moves authentication tokens from query parameters to the X-Rebar-Token HTTP header (which access logs do not record) for both endpoints, with a redaction filter as a backstop for query-string tokens.

The /rerun runbook recipe must be rewritten to use the header form instead of instructing operators to put tokens in URLs, with a note that previously-logged tokens are compromised and must be rotated separately.
The rotation of the compromised GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN must be tracked and recorded explicitly as completed before the code fix lands, ensuring the new token is not logged on first use.
